title: Research: Python shell with a Rust core, one package, bundled Postgres
goal: The kb answers, from official sources, how one Python package with a Rust core is built, pinned and operated: uv workspaces, uv.lock and a uv-managed pinned CPython, maturin and PyO3 abi3 wheels and the linux amd64 and arm64 and macOS arm64 matrix, publishing wheels and an sdist to a private GitLab PyPI registry and pinning them by version and digest, ruff and mypy --strict and clippy -D warnings as gates, pytest with testcontainers Postgres and criterion benchmarks, bundled PostgreSQL binaries shipped as a wheel and run by the package (init, start, stop, upgrade by dump and restore), SQLAlchemy 2 async with asyncpg, Alembic expand-and-contract migrations across a minor, Postgres advisory locks as single-writer invariants, pgvector, pgcrypto, canonical dumps that hash byte-identically, nightly age-encrypted dumps and git bundles to S3-compatible storage with restore tested in CI, Typer CLIs that never prompt without a TTY and print JSON, FastAPI capability-per-route decorators, SSE streams with cursors, per-caller rate limits with Retry-After, and a single-process service composing roles by flag.

gates.question: Approve this sprint's goal and committed items?
